newsitem.title: INDIA: India parliament to debate trust vote against PM.
newsitem.headline: India parliament to debate trust vote against PM.

text.p: The Indian parliament will debate a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government on Friday, lower house speaker Purno Sangma said.
"There is a no-confidence motion. We will take it up on the 21st (of February)," he told reporters on Thursday.
The motion has been moved by George Fernandes of the socialist Samta Party, a breakaway group of Deve Gowda's Janata Dal party, politicians said.

The Samta Party has an alliance with the main opposition rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the eastern state of Bihar. The BJP, which with its allies has 194 votes in the 545-seat lower house, said it will back the motion.
Deve Gowda's minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies in the Lok Sabha, or lower house. But it has been reluctantly supported by the Congress party which has 142 votes.

Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters on Wednesday that he expects the government to survive the three-month long budget session which was to start on Thursday morning, suggesting Congress, despite veiled threats to Deve Gowda, was not planning to bring down the government immediately.
